findings.creator: creator-economy
findings.topic: The 2021 video-essay format is dead and you can see it die inside the videos
findings.title: The schema can type a proxy perfectly and has no field that says it is a proxy - no fact declares the variable it stands in for
findings.expected: A quantity admitted as evidence for a claim about a different quantity is marked as such, so a reader can see the substitution without re-deriving it.
findings.got: f-lds-length measures uploaded duration (35 to 28 minutes, Dec 2024 to May 2025). My claim is about time-to-thesis. The amended schema let me state `unit: minutes`, `period`, `denominator`, `subject`, `event_date`, `evidence_class: aggregator`, `confidence: low` with a three-part note, and `qualifies: [f-no-thesis-series]` - every one of which I filled honestly and NONE of which says 'this is not the variable the claim is about'. I had to put it in a `note`, in prose, which is the field the schema itself calls a research note rather than script-ready structure. Demonstrated live in scale_conversions: 'seven minutes off the front of a half-hour - about the length of the cold open the argument is supposed to be about' is accurate, vivid, and silently promotes a total-duration claim into a cold-open claim. `for` links the conversion to the fact; nothing links the fact to the variable it substitutes for, so the subject-class rule at NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:150-154 (which catches address-cohort to 'people') cannot see a duration-to-position promotion at all.
findings.refuter_pass: 1) Is this my topic being hard? No - it is general, and it is the shape of most bad quantitative journalism: response rate for satisfaction, arrests for crime, duration for structure. My topic only makes it unmissable because the gap between the two variables is total. 2) Would competent execution catch it anyway? I caught it, so yes, a careful researcher can. But the schema's whole thesis (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:1-10) is that a rule with no field is a comment - and this rule has no field, so by the document's own standard it is a comment. 3) Is `qualifies[]` the home? No. `qualifies` is a fact-to-fact edge; the proxy relation is fact-to-VARIABLE and the variable is often unmeasured, so there is no sibling id to point at. That asymmetry is the finding. 4) content, mechanism or lens? mechanism - it is a missing field on facts[] and it is wrong for everyone.
findings.proposed_fix: `facts[].stands_for?: {variable: string, why_substituted: string}` on any quantity admitted as evidence for a claim about a different quantity, plus a quality-bar row: a load-bearing claim supported only by a `stands_for` fact is flagged.

findings.creator: creator-economy
findings.topic: The 2021 video-essay format is dead and you can see it die inside the videos
findings.title: The only source-quality rule with teeth is scoped to QUANTITATIVE facts, so a numberless notebook's entire load-bearing set is exempt from it by construction
findings.expected: The primary-source requirement applies to whatever the argument rests on, in whatever form the domain's evidence takes.
findings.got: RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:185 and NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md Rule 4 both read 'every load-bearing QUANTITATIVE fact reaches a primary source, or carries a named gap'. My four load-bearing facts are f-interior-unreachable (an absence), f-no-thesis-series (an absence), f-geller-length (an utterance) and f-solomons-counter (an utterance), plus f-midroll-threshold and f-discourse-dates. Not one is quantitative. The notebook therefore satisfies the rule completely while resting on one podcast write-up, one student-newspaper opinion column and a set of search-engine snippets - and the checklist goes green. The bar fires hardest on the domain that already has the best-instrumented sources and does not fire at all on the domain with the worst. Adopted E4 documents evidence_class as REQUIRED but RECERTIFY.md:112 already concedes 'nothing enforces them at write time'; this is the same ceiling with a scope qualifier that makes the non-enforcement invisible rather than merely unenforced.
findings.refuter_pass: 1) By design? Arguable - the scar that forced the rule (77,800 vs 270,000 BTC) was quantitative, and rules are usually written to their scar. But the RECURRENCE is the point: this is the deflated L1 finding CE-07, which I filed `uncertain` because I could only see a vacuously-passed Phase 5 row. Executing the run showed the vacuous pass is real and lives one rule over. Recurrence 2 against the same underlying complaint - non-numeric evidence gets no craft obligation - reaching a different, load-bearing rule. 2) Would competent execution catch it? No. Competent execution PASSES it. That is the defect: the checklist rewards me for having the weakest sources in the run. 3) mechanism, not content: deleting one word ('quantitative') changes the rule for every seat.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop 'quantitative'. If the intent was that only numbers can be traced to a record, that is false - an utterance traces to the recording, an absence traces to the register searched, and both are stateable in `sources[].locator`.

findings.title: An asserted absence is unguarded - the schema requires search_scope on a fact[] absence and nothing requires it of the same assertion made in the argument
findings.expected: A claim that no literature exists is held to the same standard wherever it appears.
findings.got: Phase 1 and the amended `kind: "absence"` + `search_scope` machinery discipline an absence RECORDED AS A FACT beautifully - I used it twice this run and it forced me to state what I searched and what would count as the absence lifting. But my L1 report asserted, in prose, 'nobody publishes the video essay format is fine - there is no literature', built a whole finding on it, and nothing anywhere required me to state a search scope for that assertion, because it was not a fact card. One search refuted it: Noah Solomons, The Link, 2026-03-11, 'Don't blame the video essay' - a dated published defence that concedes 'are video essays becoming formulaic? Probably' and locates the cause in the attention economy rather than the form. THE METHODIC WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ME. Phase 1 says record it as a dated absence with search_scope; had I obeyed that at L1 I would have had to search, and the search finds it in one query. The gap is that the discipline attaches to a notebook field and the assertion escaped through prose.
findings.refuter_pass: 1) Is this a finding about the methodic or about me? BOTH, and I am filing it because the methodic comes out well and I do not. The honest headline is that L1's charitable reading ran in the direction nobody budgeted for: not 'the instruction is better than it looks' but 'the CREATOR asserted a fact about the world from the armchair and the level had no way to stop him'. rubric.md:141-143 tells the judge to ask whether a competent execution of the existing prompt would have produced the finding anyway - here a competent execution DESTROYS the L1 finding. 2) Downgraded to minor because the fix is small and the mechanism mostly works. 3) It is mechanism rather than content because it is a rule about where a discipline attaches, and it applies to every seat that asserted an absence at L1 without searching - which the judge should now count.
findings.proposed_fix: One line in the Gauntlet's own instruments, not the pipeline: an L1 seat may not assert a domain absence it has not searched; it states it as a hypothesis for L2. Sibling target: rubric.md's refuter pass gains 'did the Creator assert an absence without a search scope?'

findings.title: E3's emptyByOmission/notApplicable split works and nothing computes which one applies - the reviewer self-reports, and the flattering string is always available
findings.expected: Confirmation that the alarm is no longer wired to the drain, with a named residual.
findings.got: THE FIX WORKS, and this finding is its ceiling rather than its refutation. Verified live: I derived my own seven domains per Phase 1, so `the-number` never rendered; UNTAGGED_DIMENSION held zero cards and per columnsFor() did not render; and my spine column read `emptyByOmission` - an accusation, correctly aimed at me. The residual: `Dimension` carries both strings and NOTHING SELECTS BETWEEN THEM. I chose `emptyByOmission` for `structure-in-the-cut` and `corpus-baseline`. I could have chosen `notApplicable` - I wrote that column's own notApplicable string myself, at the same keyboard, and had I written it as 'this format's structure is not measurable at scale' instead of 'never for this topic', the run would render as complete rather than as unstarted. Guardrail 3 requires the author to write both strings; nothing requires the author to be the one who cannot pick.
findings.ceiling: The split is a vocabulary, not a gate. A column's empty state is whichever of two author-written strings the author picks, and one of them says the run is fine. The only mechanical signal available - does this column have zero cards - is exactly the signal that could not distinguish the two conditions in the first place, which is why the split was needed. Closing it needs something the column can be checked against: the derived domain declaring at Phase 1 time whether it is expected to fill, before the researcher knows whether it did.
findings.refuter_pass: Checked hard against my own interest, because this is my L1 headline finding and I would rather it had survived. It did not, and I am saying so: the drain is disconnected, the alarm is reconnected, and the ceiling is a different and smaller thing. Per RECERTIFY.md's own honest summary ('the methodic now says the right things and enforces almost none of them'), this is that sentence in its mildest form - and mild is a genuine improvement on 'structurally impossible', which is what it was at L1.

findings.title: An `absence` card populates the column whose emptiness it reports - the column dial counts cards and does not read facts[].kind
findings.expected: A column holding only cards that say 'there is nothing here' reads as empty, or at minimum reads differently from a column holding two pieces of evidence.
findings.got: My spine column `structure-in-the-cut` holds exactly two cards, f-interior-unreachable and f-no-thesis-series, both `kind: "absence"`, and both of which exist to say the column is empty. Filed anywhere else they would be mis-filed - they ARE about that column. So the column renders with a count of 2 and never reaches its `emptyByOmission` string at all, because the string fires on occupancy and the column is occupied. This is the L1 finding's exact shape - a diagnostic column structurally prevented from reading empty - surviving E3 through a different door, and this time the researcher digs it himself by correctly obeying the schema. E4 gave the fact a `kind` and E3 gave the column two strings, and the two edits do not talk to each other: nothing in the empty-state logic reads `kind`. NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:20 says `absence` 'renders on the boundary rail' - which is a render decision the column dial does not inherit.
findings.refuter_pass: 1) Is this the same finding as L1's CE-02, re-filed? No, and the distinction is why it is worth a new id. CE-02 was 'an untagged card falls into a domain column'; the fix retired the fallback. This is 'a correctly-tagged card of a specific kind falsely satisfies a column' - a different mechanism, opposite cause (obedience rather than omission), same consequence. Recurrence 2 is set against the CONSEQUENCE, per rubric.md's ranking rule, because a gap returning unchanged through a new door is exactly what recurrence is for. 2) Is it my topic being exotic? No - every conflict-OSINT 'no footage exists of X', every fraud 'the register contains no such filing' is an absence card that lands in the column it empties. `conflict-osint` and `public-co-fraud` should be checked for convergence. 3) Would competent execution avoid it? Only by mis-filing the absence somewhere it does not belong, which the schema correctly forbids. There is no compliant way to avoid this.
findings.proposed_fix: The column dial counts cards where `kind !== 'absence'`, and a column whose only cards are absences renders its `emptyByOmission`/`notApplicable` state WITH the absence cards attached as the reason. That is strictly more informative than either current outcome.

findings.title: `evidence_class` attaches to the source and the class is a property of the source-claim pair - and there is no class for 'the reader can check this and I did not'
findings.expected: A single artefact cited for two different kinds of claim carries the right class for each, and a source the researcher has not verified is distinguishable from one he has.
findings.got: TWO halves, both demonstrated in this notebook. (a) A YouTube video is `primary` when the claim is about its own structure - the record IS the artefact - and `self-published` when the claim is about what its creator asserts. Same URL, two classes, and `sources[].evidence_class` has one slot per source, so the class silently becomes a property of the citation rather than of the edge. My sources[] lists two youtube.com entries as `self-published` because that was true of what I could actually get; had I watched them they would have been `primary` for the structural claim without the URL changing. (b) `protected` is defined as 'true, verified by the researcher, and not citable by the reader'. My topic's native state is the exact inverse - trivially citable by the reader, NOT verified by the researcher - and there is no class for it. That inverse is not exotic: it is every claim about a public artefact the run did not open, which after this run I would guess is common and invisible.
findings.refuter_pass: Filed `uncertain`, deliberately, and half of it should probably be refuted. Half (a) is arguably fine: sources[] is per-fact, so the same URL cited on two facts genuinely can carry two classes, and my complaint is really that the top-level sources[] bibliography then contradicts itself - which is a rendering problem, not a taxonomy one. Half (b) is the real one and it is small: I could express 'unverified by me' in confidence_note and did. Recorded at minor because the honest test is whether ANY seat needed it, and I am one seat. If nobody else reaches for it, refute it.
findings.proposed_fix: None proposed. This one should be held until a second seat hits it - E4's own recurrence note is about a rule adopted with no home, and adding a taxonomy value on one seat's word is the opposite error.
